claim: Linear difference-of-means probes on residual-stream activations of six diffusion code models read pass/fail within-problem above chance, with depth-curve peaks about 0.68 (Stable-DiffCoder) to 0.82 (LLaDA-flash).
stance_target: L2: hidden-state probes carry code-correctness signal, extended to non-autoregressive models
scope_conditions: MBPP+ , within-problem grouped 5-fold AUC, Sec 4.1, Fig 2
quoted_support: Every diffusion model in the family comparison has a peak AUC above 0.5. The depth curves peak at approximately 0.68 for Stable-DiffCoder and 0.82 for LLaDA-flash, the endpoints of the range.

claim: Probe has no consistent advantage over the model's own confidence: DiffuCoder probe AUC 0.842 vs 0.838 negative token entropy and 0.798 masked-forward; Qwen2.5-Coder probe 0.677 vs 0.703 log-probability.
stance_target: L2: probe-beats-readout claim (contrary evidence to Ribeiro et al.)
scope_conditions: Table 1, mixed problems only; DiffuCoder comparison uses only 19 problems
quoted_support: Model confidence is thus a competitive baseline for the correctness readout.

claim: Steering along the probe direction does not improve code: pass@1 0.433 baseline, 0.429 random directions, 0.388 toward pass, 0.298 toward fail; follow-up 15/30 baseline vs 14/30 positive and 5/30 negative.
stance_target: L2: causal/steering use of correctness probe
scope_conditions: DiffuCoder-7B, 30 evaluation tasks, Sec 4.4, Fig 4, App D
quoted_support: Pass@1 is 0.433 without intervention, 0.429 averaged over random directions, 0.388 when pushed toward the passing direction, and 0.298 when pushed toward the failing direction (Fig. 4).

claim: Small semantic mutations (e.g. < to <=) keep the probe AUC at 0.670 (392 MBPP+ mutants) and 0.692 (334 HumanEval+ mutants), supporting a link to correctness rather than surface style.
quoted_support: DiffuCoder distinguishes the resulting pass/fail pairs with AUCs of 0.670 on 392 MBPP+ mutants and 0.692 on 334 HumanEval+ mutants.

claim: Authors disclose statistical limits: layer chosen by max out-of-fold AUC without holdout, bootstrap merges repeated problem ids, so only point estimates are compared.
quoted_support: We therefore compare point estimates rather than make significance or equivalence claims from those uncertainty estimates.
